clue.text: Mistake made by backward schoolchildren

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for schoolchildren from right to left

parts.note: schoolchildren are pupils

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by slow learners in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like a description of slow pupils, but it is the reversal signal: PUPILS turned round gives SLIPUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an everyday word for an error or blunder.

clue.text: Landowner offering hideaway to duke

parts.note: a lair is an animal's hidden den

explanation.surface: An estate owner provides a nobleman with a hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Kissing top body builder?

parts.note: a pec, the chest muscle, is what bodybuilders build
the king is the top figure

explanation.surface: Smooching a champion weightlifter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'top body builder' as the king of pecs: PEC plus KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecking is giving a quick light kiss.

clue.text: Looking ahead, arranging Devon trip

indicators.note: arranging shows the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Planning a holiday in the West Country well in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being provident means planning for the future, thrifty and forward-thinking.

clue.text: Frontiersman given reprimand in court

indicators.note: in places the reprimand inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A pioneer of the American West gets a dressing-down from a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting 'a rocket' is British informal for being reprimanded. Davy Crockett was the famous American frontiersman.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Crockett was a celebrated American pioneer and frontier hero who died at the Alamo.

clue.text: Reconsidered Carol's opportune alternative suggestion

indicators.note: reconsidered implies the letters are thought through again into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Carol's timely offer was rethought.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterproposal is an alternative plan offered in reply to another.

clue.text: Character finally captured by fearsome gang

indicators.note: captured by means the letters are held inside the words fearsome gang

explanation.surface: A villain at last caught by a frightening mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of the Greek alphabet, so 'Character finally' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Funds to provide player's strip at important matches

parts.note: a player's kit is his uniform or strip
ties are cup matches in British sport

explanation.surface: Money raised to buy shirts for big games.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a knockout match; strip is the team uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitties are pooled sums of money, shared funds.

clue.text: At school gala, announced cost of ticket

parts.note: to school is to train or teach

indicators.note: announced means the word is to be spoken so the sound gives a different spelling

parts.note: a fair is a gala or fete

explanation.surface: At a school fete someone declares the price of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Train fare is the price paid for a railway ticket.

clue.text: Revelation girl's finally in the club? Absolutely right

indicators.note: in puts the chosen letter inside the word for a club

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word girl

parts.note: saying 'Sure!' means absolutely, you are right

explanation.surface: A shocking confession: the girl is pregnant, and it is quite true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, which drives the surface; here it means L goes inside DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure is something made known that was secret, a revelation.

clue.text: Players drink before start of match

parts.note: tea is a common drink

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of the word match

explanation.surface: Sportsmen have a cuppa before the game kicks off.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of players who compete together.

clue.text: Running modern cars with type of engine that mustn't get cold inside

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the modern era of dating
Minis are small British cars

indicators.note: mustn't get says a letter must be kept out of the engine word
inside shows the barred letter is taken from the middle of the engine word

parts.note: a traction engine is a steam-powered road vehicle
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Advice about modern cars whose engines must be kept warm.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (the present era) plus MINIS, then TRACTION with its C removed from the middle, giving TRATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The running of an organisation is its administration or management.

clue.text: Young farm animal that is touched by plague

parts.note: to dog someone is to plague or pester them
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A calf that has caught some disease on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touched by' just sets the two pieces side by side. A dogie is a motherless calf in the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: In cowboy usage a dogie is a motherless or stray calf on the range.

clue.text: A young man's upset about damages in religious building

indicators.note: about puts the reversed pair around the word for damages
upset in a down clue means the letters turn upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man
harms means damages

explanation.surface: A youth is distressed over vandalism to a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads the young man backwards, as this is a down clue; the 's is a link meaning 'is'. A dharmsala is a pilgrims' rest house in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dharmsala is an Indian rest house for pilgrims, often a religious building.

clue.text: Back troubles beginning to hamper a wife: transport needed

parts.note: ricks are sprains or strains, typically of the back

indicators.note: beginning to selects only the opening letter of the word hamper

explanation.surface: A man with a bad back and a wife in tow needs a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person, a form of transport.

clue.text: Catholic college is to receive best possible mark for religious instruction

indicators.note: to receive means the group takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
A is the top grade
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A Catholic school will get top grades in RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of doctrine taught by question and answer.

clue.text: Girl dug earth out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A child digs soil out of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, a girl in relation to her parents.

clue.text: Folk singer oddly glum before Reith broadcast

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of glum
broadcast suggests the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gloomy musician performs before a famous BBC man goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC, hence 'broadcast'. Woody Guthrie was an American folk singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Guthrie was a leading American folk musician.

clue.text: Move a piece of furniture

definitions.meaning: to ... a motion is to propose it formally at a meeting
a flat-topped stand with legs for eating or working

explanation.definitionFit: To table a proposal is to move it formally, and a dining table is a common piece of furniture.

clue.text: Tough one engaged by British employer

indicators.note: engaged by places the numeral inside the other pieces

parts.note: a user is one who employs something
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hard man is hired by a British firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big, aggressive man, a thug or tough.

clue.text: Is into computer-generated films

indicators.note: generated hints the letters are produced afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Something gets fed into a computer to make movies with CGI.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes computer-generated imagery in cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion pictures is a formal term for films or movies.

clue.text: Black suit initially discarded in card game

indicators.note: discarded means a letter is thrown away

parts.note: sombre means dark or black

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of suit

explanation.surface: A dark suit is thrown out before a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre is an old Spanish card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is a three-handed trick-taking card game popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Recall sanction introduced by first lady

indicators.note: introduced by means placed inside the name of the first lady

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
to OK is to approve or sanction

explanation.surface: The President's wife brings in a measure to be revoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to bring a memory to mind.

clue.text: Standard recipe for salmon or trout

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe

explanation.surface: A normal cooking method for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recipe' is not about cooking: R abbreviates it on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon or trout in its early freshwater stage.

clue.text: Winner at Crufts, perhaps? He isn't festooned with bows

indicators.note: festooned suggests letters draped and rearranged around one another

explanation.surface: A man without decorative ribbons seems unlikely to win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's famous annual dog show. 'With' is a link joining the two fodder pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The top prize at a dog show goes to the overall champion, the dog judged finest of every breed.

clue.text: I'll be seeing you in distant Surrey location

parts.note: distant means far
Ewell is a town in Surrey, a county south of London

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to someone heading to a remote part of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Ewell is a town in Surrey, a county bordering south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I'll be seeing you' is a parting phrase, as is a goodbye.

clue.text: Noticed vessel in the sea near Nice

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the sea's short name

parts.note: Nice lies on the Mediterranean, the Med
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A boat was spotted off the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked can mean observed or noted, as in 'he marked her absence'.
